hints: Remember stereoisomerism means either optical isomerism from a chiral carbon, or cis-trans isomerism across a C=C double bond.
Look for a carbon with four different groups attached in option A, and look for C=C bonds with two different groups at each end in options B and D.
Check the remaining saturated chain carefully to see if any carbon has four different groups and if any double bond is present at all.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two ways to get stereoisomers**

Think like a detective looking for two clues. Optical isomerism needs a chiral centre, a carbon with four different groups. Cis-trans isomerism needs a C=C double bond where each C has two different groups.

Rule to use:
$$\text{chiral C} = \text{C attached to 4 different atoms/groups}$$

**Test option A for optical isomerism**

Draw out $\text{CH}_3\text{CHClCH}_2\text{CHO}$. The second carbon is attached to $\text{H}$, $\text{Cl}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$.

That is four different groups, so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism.

**Test options B and D for cis-trans isomerism**

Option B is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$, but-2-ene. Each C of the double bond has $\text{H}$ and $\text{CH}_3$, so cis and trans forms exist.

Option D is $\text{CHCl=CHCl}$, 1,2-dichloroethene. Each C of the double bond has $\text{H}$ and $\text{Cl}$, so cis and trans forms exist.

**Test the remaining compound**

Option C is $\text{CH}_2\text{ClCH}_2\text{CHCl}_2$, which is fully saturated so no C=C for cis-trans isomerism.

Check each carbon: $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ has two H, $\text{CH}_2$ has two H, $\text{CHCl}_2$ has two Cl. No carbon has four different groups, so no chiral centre and no stereoisomerism.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHClCH}_2\text{CHO}$ contains a chiral centre at the CHCl carbon, bonded to H, Cl, CH3 and CH2CHO. It therefore shows optical isomerism.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ is but-2-ene with a C=C bond. Each alkene carbon carries H and CH3, so cis (Z) and trans (E) isomers are possible.
options.C: Correct. $\text{CH}_2\text{ClCH}_2\text{CHCl}_2$ has no C=C bond and no carbon with four different groups. With no chiral centre and no restricted rotation, it cannot show optical or cis-trans isomerism.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CHCl=CHCl}$ is 1,2-dichloroethene with a C=C bond. Each alkene carbon carries H and Cl, so cis and trans isomers are possible.
